mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is held constant for two consecutive months above 5.25%, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be positive due to reduced policy-induced discounting of future earnings.
regime_hint: FOMC holds rates steady in a restrictive environment
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during similar non-hold periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) below the prior month's value triggers a short-term decline in investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
regime_hint: Labor market softening before a recession
failure_condition: Over 20 triggered events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from baseline (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) of at least 3% for two consecutive months is associated with stronger consumer confidence and higher S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥3% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Resuming or accelerating housing market expansion
failure_condition: In regimes matching the trigger, 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 95th percentile of prior non-expansion months (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in a month coincides with a negative interaction effect on S&P 500 20-day forward returns when combined with a rising CPIAUCSL.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >5% in a month AND CPIAUCSL rises in the same month
regime_hint: Supply shock in a cost-inflationary environment
failure_condition: Across 30 such events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during comparable non-shock periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: During a 3-month decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4%, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be positive due to easing liquidity constraints.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls continuously for 3 consecutive months below 4%
regime_hint: Early signs of labor market recovery
failure_condition: Over 10 such episodes, the 5-day forward returns are not higher than the mean of prior tight-labor periods (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden jump in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of at least 10% in a month coincides with a positive 20-day forward return for the S&P 500, reflecting strong labor market momentum.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥10% in a single month
failure_condition: Across 15 such events, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during pre-jump months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (GDPC1) above 2% suggest resilient consumer demand, predicting a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by >2% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: Sustained demand recovery in a post-pandemic environment
failure_condition: In 50 such demand expansion episodes, the 60-day forward returns are not higher than the 90th percentile of baseline periods (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer spending (CPIAUCSL) by more than 2% in a month combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by 4% produces a negative interaction effect on the S&P 500 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls >2% in a month AND INDPRO falls >4% in the same month
regime_hint: Dual contraction in consumption and production (demand-supply shock)
failure_condition: Over 20 such dual contractions, the 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during comparable single-variable shocks (p > 0.10).
